summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 3, part 132) in which the narrator confronts a man, Alex Goddard, about Sarah, a troubled young woman who came to Quetzal Manor in New York wanting a child conceived without a man, believing it would be a divine child of cosmic energy. Goddard recounts how he began working with Sarah, discovered she had a rare uterine abnormality affecting about one woman in twenty thousand, and at first agreed to her wish to come to Baalum, the place of miracles, on terms she would have to keep, before regretting the offer and forbidding her to come. The narrator reflects on her childhood memory of Sarah's questions about chicks and babies and on her own guilt and similar desire for a miracle.
one_line: In a novel excerpt, Alex Goddard explains to the narrator how Sarah sought a miraculous conception at Baalum, the place of miracles.
key_facts: Sarah first appeared at Quetzal Manor in New York as a very troubled young woman.
Sarah declared she was a person of pure spirit and wanted to have a baby without touching a man.
Sarah wanted a divine child created of cosmic energy.
Goddard says Sarah was born with an abnormality of the uterus that afflicts about one woman in twenty thousand.
Sarah declared she wanted to come to Baalum, the place of miracles.
Goddard told Sarah that miracles can sometimes transpire at Baalum, but only at a great price.
Goddard said an agreement would be required and Sarah would have to keep it no matter what.
Goddard says he immediately regretted the offer because Sarah was far too unstable for this environment.
Goddard finally forbade Sarah to come to Baalum.
Just before Goddard's next scheduled trip, Sarah found out and booked herself a trip.
The narrator recalls that when Sarah was six, she asked whether human babies hatched from eggs like chicks, and declared that all living things came directly from God.
The narrator first met Goddard on a morning overlooking the bluffs of the Hudson.
The narrator sought Goddard's help seeking a miracle when all else had failed.
The narrator feels guilt about Sarah and wonders why Sarah did not come home to her and Lou.
